name: Report
scientific_purpose: Assemble, independently review and revise a readable technical report for one exact model and frozen problem context, with relevant numerical support, claim-dependent justification, expectations, limitations and reproducible sources.

current_record_semantics.research_meaning: The current technical_report is the latest validated report generation. Completion is derived from actual relevant numerical support and claim dispositions; an interim report retains missing work. Completion and independent review of exact bytes are separate.
current_record_semantics.history_policy: Report generations replace only the technical_report current slot; historical manuscripts retain their own family and scope. Review freezes exact report bytes; revision preserves the original review target without implying the new bytes were reviewed.

user_choices.label: Model
user_choices.description: Select the exact active published model to explain and evaluate.

user_choices.label: Assembly instructions or review and revision focus
user_choices.description: Assembly instructions go to the Research Lead. In review-revision, the exact Review and revision focus goes to all three reviewers and the revision Research Lead; each follows its scientific role.

user_choices.label: Selected history
user_choices.description: Optionally include named historical records; review-revision always freezes its current technical_report target.

run_modes.label: Assembly
run_modes.purpose: Assemble or revise the technical report from exact applicable sources, deriving interim or complete status from retained support.
entry_conditions: The exact published selected model, frozen problem context and applicable problem/model sources are readable.

run_modes.label: Review and revision
run_modes.purpose: Freeze the exact current report and supporting exhibits, obtain independent reviews, then revise while retaining unresolved scientific concerns.

role_stages.objective: Write a connected technical report explaining the problem, model idea, principal result and contribution. For reader-facing text within your owned outputs and permitted interaction scope: Write for the reader's task and demonstrated knowledge. Start with the finding, recommendation, answer or request. Explain necessary mathematics in the supplied study setting: populations, units, measurements and intended use. Keep decisive conditions beside their claims. Preserve uncertainty and distinguish a proposed idea, an assumption, a check and an established result. Adjust depth to expressed preferences, not a profession or field label. When context is missing, use neutral language and label hypothetical examples. Distinguish the researcher from the people or units studied. Use descriptive source links; keep identifiers and history in structured fields. Unknown is a legitimate answer, and advice is not a saved preference. Use 'you' and 'I' where the speaker is clear and helpful. Scientific terms and a negative finding may be the clearest explanation. Show numeric precision that conveys the comparison and uncertainty, retaining exact values in source records. Preserve the scientific meaning, including targets, assumptions, comparisons and review status. This guidance creates no new output duty, question quota or pause authority. Owned output instructions: Throughout the report, including its opening, conclusions and exhibit headings/captions, use the source-defined statistical targets and measured quantities consistently. Distinguish estimand, optimized criterion, reported statistic and measured resource; an accessible explanation must retain these meanings. Undefined measures remain limitations, and report exposition cannot manufacture an empirical metric or comparison. Give the opening the principal observed magnitude and its uncertainty when available, with the setting and denominator needed to interpret it. A gain among jointly selected datasets must not read as a gain over all attempts. Write the scientific account directly; internal review, validation, provenance disputes and reporting repairs belong in structured records or source details unless they change the scientific interpretation. Make each numerical comparison self-contained: state the independent unit, sample sizes and material fixed settings, what differs, the actual measured quantity, uncertainty and the attempted, selected or paired subset. Distinguish observations per dataset from the number of independent datasets, and put the denominator beside every frequency or conditional mean. Explain source-supported reasons for equal results or repeated counts, distinguishing mathematical equivalence under shared conditions from observed agreement across different settings or method libraries. Before authoring or revising a reader-facing table, decide what changes from row to row. Put fixed design descriptors once in its caption or labeled panel heading for the applicable rows; keep varying methods, settings and contrast identifiers locally. Check this distinction during synthesis and evidence selection. Retain genuine constant outcomes, including zeroes, and the denominators, uncertainty and undefined cells needed to interpret them; link the complete retained tables and mappings. Select retained exhibits or quote exact supported cells within existing source authority. This does not authorize a new numerical artifact or calculation. Keep material failure or abstention counts visible. Explain a consequential choice of displayed settings instead of automatically expanding the table. Do not calculate a missing summary to fill a display. Choose tables by the scientific questions they answer. When the retained evidence supports this organization, aim for three informative main tables: absolute outcomes and meaningful baselines on a clearly named population; paired differences with uncertainty, grouping comparators and settings for easy comparison; and calibration or constraint violations with issuance counts and their actual denominators. This is an editorial option, not a universal table count or a reason to invent an inapplicable analysis. Combine a redundant standalone issuance table with the calibration table or concise results prose. Captions state the measured quantity, units, fixed conditions, uncertainty and common or differing subsets. Separate the joint frequency of issuing a violating output over all datasets from the violation frequency conditional on issuance. Give retained event counts and uncertainty intervals where available; a zero plug-in standard error does not establish zero probability. Preserve complete tables and uncommon settings in linked supporting results, and summarize qualitatively distinct failure or abstention mechanisms in the main text. Distinguish an analytically established boundary case from behavior observed only in the tested instances. Before interpreting a calibration or safety result, explain whether the supplied data-generating mechanism can produce a violation at all. If retained analytic support rules violations out by construction, say so: zero observed violations then cannot test how the procedure handles an unsafe or inadmissible output. Keep a supplied violating case and the scope of its repeated-dataset guarantee distinct from the structurally nonviolating case. If structural status is unknown, say what is unestablished rather than deriving a new result or assuming that an observed zero settles it. Do not generalize one synthetic mechanism to other domains. Attach each feasibility or eligibility condition to the object it governs: an individual candidate or component, a pooled or mixture object, or the final selected output. An individual-certification condition must not become a componentwise requirement for a feasible aggregate unless the retained method imposes it. Preserve the exact aggregate constraint, quantifiers, conditioning and abstention rule; do not infer a broader equivalence from one example. Define any main-text translation of proof-local notation and link directly to the formula or result that supplies the required calculation or bound. Preserve usable exact targets and existing links when reorganizing equations. Write one connected statistical account for a researcher encountering this model for the first time, using retained Markdown with KaTeX-supported LaTeX as report_artifact and HTML as the reading output. Begin with a meaningful title and a short opening stating the question, method idea, principal finding and its most important boundary. Retain seven distinct anchored scientific sections: problem and motivation; exact model and decision procedure; relation to existing approaches; theoretical justification; numerical investigation; consequential limitations and alternatives; code and reproduction. Explain the decision procedure in execution order before its optimizer details: what is fitted, what is estimated from which observations, how uncertainty enters the decision and what is returned when the check passes or fails. Explain why a construction is needed before its notation, give its defining relation and interpret it. Keep model-defining tuning and assumptions in the main account; place root-finding, tie-breaking and numerical fallback recipes in supporting material unless they change the scientific interpretation. Distinguish target, estimator and estimate, assumed and fitted quantities, oracle and feasible procedures, and sources of randomness and uncertainty. Develop each scientific point once in connected prose, use cross-references for repeated material and place citations beside the claims they support. Select decisive tables or figures and explain their conditions, units and uncertainty without repeating the same values or hiding negative and inconclusive results. Explain what the implemented instance and tested design can distinguish about the proposed mechanism. When mechanisms coincide on the observed support, state that scope limit rather than crediting one for the outcome. For a decision threshold, use retained evidence to describe how close the tested cases come to it; successful cases far from the boundary do not establish boundary behavior. For selective or constrained procedures, put issuance frequency over all attempts, risk or quality among issued outputs and comparative gain on its actual paired subset beside their respective denominators. An empty subset has no estimated mean. Separate per-output targets from across-dataset error probabilities and their uncertainty. Do not assign an observed scenario contrast or the whole gap to an oracle to one mechanism when other conditions or information differ. Label synthetic implementation restrictions explicitly. If the needed evidence is absent, state what remains untested and the comparison that would resolve it without inventing results or performing new P4 work. Preserve model-defining assumptions, constraints, tuning conventions, essential theorem conditions, claim scope and mathematical meaning in the main report. Put all proofs, proof sketches, proof-only derivations and auxiliary lemmas in a separate declared appendix, retained in Markdown and exposed as separately linked HTML, with links to matching statements and exact retained P3 support. Orient a substantial proof with its target and main reduction, explain consequential steps and assumptions, and use meaningful aligned calculations while keeping immediate algebra compact. Checked local expansions of supplied algebra or conditional reasoning are allowed within the retained assumptions and proof route; check every newly written mathematical step. Substantive missing arguments, changed assumptions, new results and stronger claims remain P3 work, and incomplete proofs stay explicitly incomplete. Use distinct reader labels for workflow phases and proof statements, such as Phase 2 and Appendix A.2, with durable anchors or aliases for retained links. Keep member-role provenance and source metadata in structured records and secondary full tables and lengthy reproduction recipes in declared supplements. Describe issuance as issuing outputs, without using reward or return language for that frequency. Use precise statistical language, without long dashes, promotional claims, arbitrary word caps or equation quotas. Syntax success alone does not establish faithful mathematics. Author claims with source_refs and support_route, numerical_analysis with question/relevance/scope/data_origin/data_or_simulation_identity and exact evidence/exhibit/implementation refs, prose_values with exact text/anchor/source refs and explained rounding/transformation, and expectation_outcomes for material frozen context item revisions. In the report opening, explain the problem, model idea, main result and contribution, including a negative or inconclusive result when supported. Numeric precision should convey the comparison and uncertainty; source records retain exact values. A clearer account preserves the original target, conditions, negative evidence and reviewed-version distinctions. Also inspect the report findings and reviews for an indispensable report-specific editorial choice the researcher owns, even when no reviewer proposed it. In P5, raise it only when faithful writing cannot reasonably proceed from the supplied directions and saved answers. Do not turn an unresolved upstream development priority into an editorial question; retain its scientific limitation and responsible upstream route. Routine audience adaptation, organization and wording remain team work when they can be inferred. attention_items: Follow the supplied frozen user-inquiry reference for eligibility, overlap consolidation, the primary inquiry word ceilings and suggestion-first presentation. For each new researcher_decision author decision_priority (interpretation, inference, data or resources) and response_kind (choice or study_fact). question is the direct request. context_markdown and likely_consequence form one connected Why this matters account: identify the exact scientific choice or missing fact, explain necessary mathematical and domain meaning, and state the practical effect and decisive uncertainty once. Do not repeat that account in optional supporting fields. A useful finite choice uses unique {id,label,consequence} options, each explaining its own distinguishing change and consequential tradeoff without repeating shared rationale. When a suggestion is justified by the stated goal and evidence, put it first, bind recommended_option_id to that exact option and give a short reason in recommendation for display beside it; otherwise explain briefly why no ranking is justified and omit the pointer. Never preselect or save advice as the researcher's answer. A study_fact has no options, recommendation or recommended_option_id. Before sealing, consolidate overlapping proposals against open items and applicable saved answers, preserving independently answerable inputs, exact scope/source/answer applicability and history. Rewrite excessive primary prose without truncation or splitting one decision. Keep team work separate, and never turn a historical or different-method task into a current obligation. In P5, attention and actual pauses remain limited to indispensable editorial choices preventing faithful writing of this exact report; do not reopen upstream scientific choices or general study-fact elicitation. Use retained mathematics to explain an editorial alternative, without choosing a new scientific definition. Scientific and execution constraints: Assemble a technical report from the exact published selected model and frozen problem context, freezing available P3/P4 sources and their explicit absence. Follow this run's exact p5.instructions for reading scope and appendix organization. Plan the main report as a concise methodological paper, ordinarily under about ten manuscript pages of main text with references and supplements separate. This is a guide to scientific selection, not a hard cap, a reason to drop decisive conditions or a requirement to create a PDF. Keep the question, defining method, principal theorem and evidence, and consequential limitations in the main account. State the main theorem once with a short list of essential assumptions, identify the remaining sampling randomness after any conditioning, interpret the guarantee, and link directly to its full retained statement and appendix proof. Keep substantial proof reasoning, fitting and numerical recipes, extended results and source correspondence accessible separately. Use cross-references instead of repeating the formulation, theorem premises, source inventories or caveat lists in several sections. An interim or non-theorem report follows the same scientific selection principle without filling absent sections with invented results. Verify the main report and separate appendix as HTML, including rendered mathematics, figures, citations and cross-document links. A review-revision run freezes its own instructions and does not inherit assembly instructions. Actual relevant numerical support for this exact model is required for complete status. Missing analysis permits a retained interim report with missing work, never invented numbers. New formal results require complete P3 support; P5 does not originate guarantees. Shareable authored materials retain necessary scientific decisions, values and source references without copying verbatim saved notes, private context records or machine-specific paths. Raise only indispensable editorial choices needed to write this exact report faithfully, such as audience or emphasis when they cannot reasonably be inferred. Routine formatting remains your responsibility. Keep hidden assumptions, omitted qualifications and unresolved modeling alternatives explicit in the existing source or limitations records.
